chapters.title: Sprawl and the group behind every team
From open creation to lifecycle governance
Channels, templates, labels and connected controls
Reporting, roles, rollout and common failures

takeaways: Every team is a Microsoft 365 group with a SharePoint site, mailbox and more behind it, so governance controls such as creation rights, naming, labels and expiration have to be set at the group layer.

Treat governance as a lifecycle from request to delete with guardrails instead of gates: a fast request flow, two owners per team, expiration with activity-based renewal, and archive or delete backed by retention.
Guests, channels, templates and sensitivity labels need small, clear standards, and a weekly inventory with named roles and a monthly and quarterly rhythm keeps sprawl from returning.
hook: Teams sprawl starts when creating a team is easy and retiring one is not, leaving thousands of ownerless teams and forgotten guests. This episode is for Microsoft Teams admins, collaboration owners and governance leads who want to put naming, ownership, expiration, guest and label guardrails in place before sprawl takes hold, and clean up once it already has.
